svg.title: Six safeguards to set before deploying an AI agent
svg.desc: An animated diagram of six safeguards to put in place before an AI agent is allowed to act: limit what it can access, restrict its permissions, separate trusted instructions from untrusted content, keep a human on high-impact actions, control how data moves between systems, and log and monitor what it does. Each one shows the question to ask and the failure it prevents. Underneath, a worked example: an agent that only needs to summarise email is granted six permissions, and the five it never needed are struck off one by one until only summarising is left. It closes on the question worth asking before any deployment — what is the worst thing this agent could do with the permissions we gave it?
svg.text: Six safeguards, before you deploy an agent
An agent that answers questions is a document. One that can act is a system.
safeguards go in before it acts

g.text: “What does this agent genuinely need access to?”
a summariser that can also send, delete and search the whole organisation
Give it the minimum access it needs to do its job.
“What is the minimum permission required to accomplish that?”
treating OAuth as a security strategy rather than a login
Authorising something is not the same as deciding what it may do.
a web page, email or document telling your agent what to do
Your instructions and the content you read are not the same channel.
sending, publishing, purchasing, deleting or executing without a person
Not approval for everything — that throws away the benefit.
“Can one system make the agent send data into another?”
legitimate access to two systems becoming a path between them
Access to both is not permission to bridge them.
“If this goes wrong, can you reconstruct what happened?”
an incident you cannot explain afterwards
What it accessed, what it tried, which tools, what it sent.
WHAT THE AGENT IS ALLOWED TO DO
What is the worst thing this agent could do with the permissions we gave it?

svg.text: least privilege · trusted instructions are not untrusted content · a human on anything that cannot be undone
